newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end slightly down in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end slightly down in quiet trade.

text.p: Manila shares closed slightly down on Wednesday as profit-taking took a holding pattern, traders said.

"We just need this correction phase because of a consecutive seven-day rise. There's no compelling negative news so the market may rebound on Friday," said Bogart Cruz, trading manager at Asia Pacific Capital Equities. The main index ended down 3.20 points, or 0.10 percent, at 3258.52.
Gainers slightly outnumbered losers at 67 to 66 with 69 issues unchanged. Trade was heavy at 11.553 billion shares, amounting to 2.608 billion pesos.

Secondliners outperformed big cap issues as most of the blue chips were steady or slightly up. "We will see more of the same tommorrow with people becoming more selective in blue-chip buying. Big cap issues may still give way to demand for secondliners," said Jonas Ferrer, research director at Pryce Securities.
Harry Liu, president at Summit Securities said that due to the market's overbought situation, the consolidation phase may persist on Thursday with the index moving within a 3,200 to 3,250 range.
